newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends lower after pounding.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends lower after pounding.

text.p: Hong Kong gold slid sharply on Thursday to end below New York's previous close after continuous selling during the day, but a shortage of gold bars in Hong Kong made physical buying almost impossible, dealers said.
Bullion ended at US$354.00/50 an ounce against New York's US$355.70/356.10 close on Wednesday.

Some bullion sources reported sales from Japan on dollar/yen movements, and others reported Australian sales. But dealers were not sure where much of the heavy selling pressure seen in afternoon trade originated from.
"It's very scary, this continuous drop," said one bullion trader, noting the market did not seem to have a bottom level.
Some bullion dealers saw two-way trade at $354.50.

Bullion dealers said they were looking for the market to start shortcovering soon, but most were uncertain about what the market was going to do after it had dropped to current unexpectedly low levels.
"I thought it would hold at $355, but now it could go to $352-353," one source said.
The shortage of kilobars in Hong Kong had almost doubled the premium for physical bullion over the spot market compared to last week, a physical gold dealer said.
